title: Enabling Unstructured Sparse Acceleration on Structured Sparse Accelerators
problem: Unstructured sparse DNN models cannot be accelerated on structured sparse hardware (e.g., 2:4 NVIDIA sparse Tensor Cores), and structured sparse models require hardware-specific fine-tuning making them non-portable.
motivation: State-of-the-art sparse accelerators support only fixed N:M structured sparsity patterns. Unstructured sparse models from pruning pipelines are incompatible with these accelerators, and retraining for each target hardware is expensive. A hardware-agnostic decomposition could unlock acceleration without retraining.
method: TASD (Tensor Approximation via Structured Decomposition): decomposes any sparse tensor into a series of N:M structured sparse tensors using the distributive property of tensor algebra. TASD-W performs offline weight decomposition via greedy layer-wise search minimizing dropped non-zeros while maintaining 99% model quality. TASD-A handles dynamic runtime activation decomposition with sparsity-degree-based pattern selection attached to accelerator input. TTC (TASD Tensor Core) extends VEGETA/STC to support multiple N:M patterns simultaneously. Decomposition-aware dataflow keeps B/C tiles stationary to amortize the decomposition overhead.
key_novelty: First method enabling unstructured sparse DNNs to run on structured sparse hardware without fine-tuning, via tensor series decomposition exploiting the distributive property of matrix algebra.
contributions: TASD decomposition framework converting arbitrary sparse tensors to series of N:M structured sparse tensors
TASD-W offline weight decomposition with greedy layer-wise quality-constrained search
TASD-A runtime activation decomposition with dynamic pattern selection
TTC hardware design supporting multiple N:M patterns on structured sparse accelerator
Decomposition-aware stationary dataflow to minimize overhead

metrics.speedup: 39% speedup on NVIDIA RTX 3080 (2:4 sparse Tensor Cores)
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: EDP improvement up to 83% (dense DNNs), 74% (sparse DNNs)
metrics.accuracy: Maintains 99% model quality target with greedy decomposition

limitations: Decomposition introduces multiple passes over structured sparse hardware
Quality guarantee (99%) is a heuristic threshold, not formal
TASD-A runtime overhead depends on sparsity pattern detection latency
